div.ab: Benedictio aquę frigidę ad iudicium faciendum.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 422 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann’s heading: [XIII.]; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “1067?–1125 (Liebermann)”, now “1067?–1125 (Liebermann, I p. 422)”)

note.seg: Hss.: Vt2 f. 191; Tr f. 179; Mg f. 211v, alle um 1130—50: daher und weil der Abendmahlswein für Laien in 4, 1 fortgelassen, ist XIII wohl nach Angelsachsenzeit in England eingeführt. Vorher geht Kesselprobe, oben XII. Am nächsten steht XIII zur Hs. aus Eichstädt bei Zeumer 653—55.

MSS: Vt2 f. 191; Tr f. 179; Mg f. 211v, all c. 1130—50: for this reason, and because the communion wine for laymen is omitted in 4, 1, XIII was probably introduced into England after the Anglo-Saxon period. It is preceded by the cauldron ordeal, above XII. XIII stands closest to the MS from Eichstädt in Zeumer 653—55.
